title: Terms and Conditions of Enrolment
notice: Draft for review. Not approved for issue or signature. The offer schedule, current policy versions and approval record must be completed before use.

sections.title: Acceptance of Offer of Enrolment
paragraphs: 1.1 An offer of enrolment must be accepted by both Parents, where appropriate, unless the College agrees to waive this requirement. Upon acceptance, all signatories will be jointly and severally liable for the obligations contained in these terms and conditions.

1.2 The offer identifies the Student, entry year and year level. Acceptance is subject to the commencement conditions in clause 2 and the Fee Schedule. No separate non-refundable acceptance fee is imposed by these terms.

1.3 A request to defer entry must be made to the College in writing. A place in another year is available only if confirmed in writing. Otherwise, the College may offer a waiting-list position; this does not guarantee a future place.
1.4 The issued offer schedule, Fee Schedule, these terms and the policies identified in this agreement form the Enrolment Agreement.

sections.title: Conditional Enrolment
paragraphs: 2.1 Before commencement, the College will consult with Parents about the Student’s needs and the support and reasonable adjustments required. Any decision about whether enrolment can proceed must comply with applicable law and the College’s enrolment procedures. A disability or need for support does not, by itself, justify refusal or cancellation.

2.2 Parents must provide accurate information and relevant existing reports or assessments reasonably needed to plan the Student’s education, health and safety. Requests will be explained and limited to information relevant to that purpose; further assessment requirements will be discussed with the family.

2.3 Where English-language support is needed, the College will discuss assessment, support and participation arrangements with the family. These terms do not impose an automatic English-proficiency exclusion or cancellation rule.

2.4 Rosewood is working towards opening in 2027. Opening and commencement remain subject to VRQA registration, applicable registration requirements and written confirmation of commencement from the College. Acceptance of this agreement does not itself confirm that the Student may commence.

2.5 No tuition, levy, bond or withdrawal charge becomes payable before those commencement conditions are confirmed as satisfied. The issued offer schedule will specify the acceptance deadline, conditions deadline and payment period after written confirmation.

2.6 If the commencement conditions are not met by the stated deadline, either party may end this agreement in writing without a withdrawal charge. Any money paid under it must be returned within the refund period stated in the offer schedule. Extending that deadline requires express written agreement.

sections.title: Needs of the Student
paragraphs: 3.1 Parents and the College will keep the Student’s learning, wellbeing and support arrangements under review. If concerns arise about meeting the Student’s needs, the College will consult the family, consider reasonable adjustments and available alternatives, and explain its assessment.

3.2 If ending enrolment is proposed on these grounds, it must be lawful and follow the notice, response and review process in clause 12. Any final decision will provide written reasons and at least one full term’s notice. Immediate protective measures for safety are separate and must be reviewed promptly.

sections.title: Fees and Charges
paragraphs: 4.1 The Board of Families for Education Ltd determines the College’s fees, levies and discounts. The published 2027 Fee Schedule for Prep to Grade 5 forms part of this agreement: tuition is $6,990 less the $1,000 Foundation Year reduction, plus a $910 Student Resource Levy, giving $6,900 per student before further tuition reductions. Subsequent-year fees and discounts will be notified in writing before the next year’s re-enrolment or withdrawal decision is required.

4.2 The $910 Student Resource Levy covers books, stationery, IT equipment, camps, excursions, incursions, specialised learning programmes/resources and student printed material. Tuition reductions do not reduce this levy. Uniforms are paid separately by families. Any genuinely additional optional charge outside these inclusions must be disclosed and agreed before participation; included items must not be charged twice.

4.3 Parents are responsible for reasonable medical or ambulance costs properly incurred for the Student where those costs are lawfully payable by them and are not met by insurance or another arrangement. This does not transfer costs arising from the College’s negligence to the family.

4.4 Tuition is invoiced at the start of each term, with payment due within 14 days. The full Student Resource Levy is invoiced at the start of Term 1 and is also due within 14 days. Families may instead pay the full annual fee at the start of Term 1 and receive a further 5% tuition reduction. Any alternative payment arrangement must be agreed in writing. Payment remains subject to the commencement conditions in clause 2.

4.5 If an amount remains unpaid 60 days after its due date, the College may commence a formal arrears review after written reminders and an opportunity to discuss the account. The College will consider disputed amounts, hardship and payment arrangements. Any proposed suspension or termination must follow clause 12; it is not automatic.

4.6 Absence because of illness, approved leave or suspension does not automatically reduce tuition fees. Parents may request a remission or hardship review. Applicable consumer rights, any agreed refund and adjustments required by law remain unaffected.

4.7 For an optional activity outside the Student Resource Levy with separately disclosed recurring charges, six weeks’ written notice is required to discontinue it only where that condition was disclosed before joining. A charge for shorter notice must reflect the unserved notice period, be lawful and not exceed six weeks’ activity fees; recoverable savings, hardship and exceptional circumstances will be considered. This clause does not create additional charges for levy-covered activities.

4.8 The refundable bond is separate from annual fees. Option A is $2,000 once per family, payable when the first child enrols, with no bond-related tuition reduction or further sibling bond. Option B is $10,000 in the first year, giving the first child a 5% tuition reduction each year at Rosewood up to Year 12. A family with two or more children may choose a second $10,000 bond, making $20,000 in total and giving every child a 5% tuition reduction. $20,000 is the maximum family bond, regardless of the number of children. The selected option and any existing bond credit must be recorded.

4.9 Option A is refunded when the last family member leaves Rosewood. Under Option B, the first $10,000 is refunded when the first child leaves; the second $10,000, if paid, is refunded when the last child leaves. Clause 2 applies if the commencement conditions are not met.

4.10 For children attending at the same time, the sibling tuition reductions are 0% for the first child, 15% for the second, 30% for the third, 45% for the fourth and 100% for the fifth and subsequent children. The $910 levy remains payable for each child. The $1,000 Foundation Year reduction applies first, followed by sibling, bond and annual-payment reductions in that order, with each percentage reduction rounded to the nearest cent. The family’s payment plan, bond choice and applicable reductions determine the final total.

sections.title: Withdrawal of Students
paragraphs: 5.1 Parents must notify the College in writing when withdrawing a Student and provide the intended leaving date. Where the Student transfers to another school, Parents should provide the destination school and entry year level to support transfer and attendance arrangements.

5.2 After the commencement conditions are satisfied, withdrawal at the end of a term requires one full school term’s written notice, received by the last day of the preceding term. The College will acknowledge the notice and confirm the financial arrangements.

5.3 Shorter notice may result in a charge for the unserved notice period’s net tuition, capped at one term, only where lawful. The College will explain the calculation and consider savings, mitigation, hardship and exceptional circumstances. There will be no double recovery.

5.4 Before commencement conditions are satisfied, clause 2 applies. After confirmation but before the Student starts, a withdrawal charge may apply only if specifically disclosed in the accepted Fee Schedule and lawful. Bond refunds follow clause 4.9.

sections.title: Obligations of Students
paragraphs: 6.1 Students are expected to follow reasonable staff directions and the College’s rules and Student Code of Conduct, with regard to their age, development and support needs.
6.2 Students must treat others courteously, respect their safety, dignity, privacy and property, and refrain from bullying, harassment and threatening behaviour.

6.3 These expectations apply to relevant online and offsite conduct. Students must not publish abusive or knowingly false material about others. Raising a concern or making a good-faith complaint is permitted.
6.4 Students are expected to respect the College’s Catholic educational ethos, values and learning environment.

6.5 Students are expected to attend and participate in scheduled assemblies, sport, College events, liturgies, camps and excursions that form part of their educational programme, subject to applicable consent, approved exemptions and reasonable adjustments.
6.6 Students must follow the published uniform and presentation requirements, including requirements applying when travelling to and from school, with any agreed adjustments or exemptions.
6.7 Students must attend during school hours unless absent through illness, approved leave or a lawful exemption. Absences must be notified through the College’s attendance process.

sections.title: Obligations of Parent/carer(s)
paragraphs: 7.1 Parents must cooperate with reasonable directions of the Principal and Board relating to the Student’s education, safety and College operations. Concerns about decisions may be raised through the College’s communication and complaints processes.
7.2 Parents are expected to support the College’s Catholic educational ethos, their child’s learning and the Parent Code of Conduct.
7.3 Parents should check College communications regularly, including newsletters, relevant policies and notified changes, and respond when action is requested.
7.4 Parents agree to support the Student’s age-appropriate compliance with the ICT Acceptable Use Agreement and other policies identified in this agreement.

7.5 Parents must promptly notify the College in writing of changes to contact details and other material enrolment information. If contact is lost, the College will make reasonable attempts to restore communication before considering further action under its procedures.
7.6 Parents must notify the College promptly when the Student is absent and provide the information reasonably required by its attendance procedures.

7.7 Parents must securely provide relevant court orders or lawful arrangements affecting parental responsibility, contact, access or the Student’s welfare, and promptly notify changes. The College will observe applicable legal restrictions.

7.8 Parents must arrange the required uniform and any disclosed learning materials not covered by the Student Resource Levy, keep them in suitable condition, and discuss hardship or adjustment needs with the College.
7.9 Parents must communicate respectfully with students, families, staff and visitors and follow the College’s communication channels.

7.10 Parents are expected to attend termly parent-mentor meetings and designated key parent functions. Where attendance is impracticable, they should arrange a reasonable alternative with the College.

7.11 Parents are encouraged to participate in family-enrichment and parent-education opportunities where offered by the College; participation is not an additional condition of enrolment under this clause.

7.12 Parents must not use social media to bully, threaten, harass or publish knowingly false allegations about members of the College community. This does not prevent respectful disagreement, good-faith complaints or contact with a regulator.

sections.title: Health and Safety
paragraphs: 8.1 Parents must promptly advise the College of material medical, physical, psychological or other support needs, and of changes affecting the Student’s wellbeing or safety. Urgent safety information should be communicated immediately.

8.2 Before commencement, Parents must confirm that the Student’s health, emergency-contact and required care information is current and complete, and provide updates when circumstances change or the College reasonably requests them.

8.3 If urgent treatment is needed and an authorised adult cannot be reached, the Principal or authorised staff member may seek first aid, an ambulance or medical assistance and give any consent they are lawfully able to give. The College will continue trying to contact the family. Costs are governed by clause 4.3; no general indemnity for the College’s negligence is given.
8.4 Parents and Students must follow applicable site-security, supervision, collection and child-safety procedures and the Child Safety Code of Conduct.

8.5 Students should care for and label their belongings and avoid bringing unnecessary valuables. The College is not an insurer of personal property; responsibility for any loss or damage remains subject to applicable law and the circumstances.

8.6 Inspection of bags, lockers or possessions may occur only where lawfully permitted under the College’s safety procedures, on reasonable grounds and with regard to the Student’s dignity and wellbeing. Parents will be informed where appropriate. This clause does not authorise an unlawful or unreasonable search.

sections.title: Programs and Activities
paragraphs: 9.1 The College determines its educational programmes, timetable and activities consistently with its published educational philosophy, curriculum obligations and applicable law.

9.2 Programmes and activities may change for educational, staffing, operational or safety reasons. The College will explain significant changes and give reasonable notice where practicable. Material changes to agreed obligations are governed by clause 13.

9.3 Students are expected to participate in compulsory curricular activities, including camps and excursions where designated, subject to required consent and reasonable adjustments. Parents seeking an exemption or alternative should discuss it with the Principal before the activity.

sections.title: Reports
paragraphs: 10.1 Academic reports will be provided through the College’s nominated secure channel using current authorised contact details. Parents should keep those details up to date.

10.2 Where Parents live separately, each Parent entitled to receive reports will ordinarily have access. The College will apply relevant court orders, legal restrictions and lawful access arrangements; one Parent’s request alone does not remove another Parent’s lawful entitlement.

sections.title: Leave
paragraphs: 11.1 Requests for planned leave from school or a scheduled academic or co-curricular activity must be made to the Principal in advance, with the dates and reason. Approval is subject to attendance obligations and the Student’s circumstances. Unexpected illness or emergencies should be reported promptly through the attendance process.

sections.title: Suspension & Termination of Enrolment
paragraphs: 12.1 Serious or repeated breaches of College rules, conduct threatening the safety or wellbeing of others, unresolved fee non-payment or other lawful grounds may lead to a suspension or termination proposal under the published procedures. Parent conduct will be considered proportionately, including reasonable alternatives and the Student’s education; a complaint or disagreement alone is not grounds for termination.

12.2 Before a final adverse decision, the College will explain the concerns and proposed action, provide a reasonable opportunity to respond, consider the Student’s circumstances and support needs, and give written reasons and review options. Urgent temporary protective measures must receive prompt review. Corporal punishment is prohibited.

12.3 Materially inaccurate or withheld information relevant to education or safety may require reassessment. The College will seek clarification and consider its significance, support options and applicable law before making a decision. This is not an automatic right to cancel enrolment without notice because a disability or support need is identified.

12.4 Parents may use the Complaints and Grievances Policy, including escalation for concerns about the Principal or procedural fairness, and may contact external authorities or exercise legal rights. Clauses 3 and 5 govern relevant notice arrangements; statutory rights remain unaffected.

sections.title: Amendment of Terms and Conditions
paragraphs: 13.1 The College will ordinarily give at least two full school terms’ written notice of proposed material changes to these terms, identifying the changes and their intended commencement. Material changes to agreed obligations require express agreement; notice or silence alone is not acceptance.

13.2 Routine administrative and policy updates may be made with reasonable notice where they do not materially change agreed obligations. Urgent changes required by law or safety will be explained as soon as practicable. Fee-setting is addressed in clause 4.1; statutory rights and review options remain available.

sections.title: Definitions
paragraphs: 14.1 College means Rosewood College, operated by Families for Education Ltd. Board means the governing board of Families for Education Ltd. Principal includes an authorised delegate where appropriate.
14.2 Parent means a parent, legal guardian or other person whose authority to enter this agreement has been accepted by the College. Student means the child identified in the offer.

14.3 Offer schedule means the child-specific place, dates and commencement conditions issued by the College. Fee Schedule means the identified schedule of tuition, levies, extras, discounts, bond arrangements, payment terms and refunds forming part of that offer.

14.4 Enrolment Agreement means the issued offer and schedules, these terms and the identified policy versions accepted by the required signatories. Nothing in it excludes rights or obligations that cannot lawfully be excluded.

## Parent Code of Conduct Policy

Exported on 30 Jun 2026
Purpose
The purpose of this policy is to set out the conduct expected of parents, guardians and carers at Rosewood College.
Rosewood College (the College) recognises parents as the primary educators of their children and seeks to work in close partnership with families. This policy supports a school community marked by trust, respect, responsibility, child safety and shared commitment to the formation of students.
This policy also supports the College’s duty of care, child safety obligations, staff wellbeing, complaints handling, student wellbeing, enrolment relationships, family engagement and the safe operation of College activities.
Scope
This policy applies to parents, guardians, carers and family members of current and prospective students.
It applies in all interactions connected with the College, including:
on College grounds
at arrival, dismissal, late arrival and early collection
at school events, meetings, liturgies, assemblies, excursions and offsite activities
during enrolment, mentoring, wellbeing, behaviour or learning discussions
in written, verbal, digital and social media communication
when communicating with staff, students, parents, volunteers, contractors, visitors or members of the wider community about College matters
when volunteering, attending events or participating in College activities
when participating in parent communication groups or informal parent networks connected with College life
Policy
Parent partnership principles
Parents and guardians are expected to support a respectful partnership between home and the College.
Parents and guardians are expected to:
uphold the dignity and safety of every student
communicate respectfully with staff and other members of the College community
support the College’s Catholic identity, philosophy, values and behaviour expectations
support the College’s Student Behaviour Management Policy and related behaviour expectations
work constructively with staff in the best interests of students
use appropriate College communication and complaint pathways
respect privacy, confidentiality and procedural fairness
comply with reasonable directions relating to safety, supervision, visitor access and College operations
model conduct that supports student formation in virtue, responsibility and respect
read and comply with College policies, procedures, handbooks and reasonable operational requirements communicated to families
respond to College communications, forms, permissions and requests for information within the timeframe requested
attend required parent functions, mentor meetings, learning discussions and other meetings requested by the College, unless alternative arrangements have been made with the College
keep the College informed of information relevant to their child’s learning, behaviour, health, safety, family circumstances or wellbeing
recognise that the College considers parent requests and new information, but cannot necessarily accommodate every request
Respectful communication
Parents and guardians must communicate with staff, students and other members of the College community in a manner that is respectful, truthful and constructive.
Unacceptable conduct includes:
aggression, intimidation, threats or harassment
abusive, insulting, discriminatory or degrading language
persistent unreasonable demands or communications
shouting, swearing or hostile behaviour
public criticism of staff, students or families in a way that undermines safety, dignity or trust
spreading rumours or confidential information
using social media to target, shame, harass or undermine staff, students, families or the College
retaliation against a person who raises a concern or complaint
Parents and guardians must recognise the damage that gossip, speculation, rumour and unconstructive commentary can cause within a school community.
Communication with staff
Parents and guardians are expected to communicate with staff through approved College channels.
Parents and guardians must:
make an appointment if they wish to meet with a staff member
use College communication channels rather than staff personal contact details or personal online accounts
respect staff working time, privacy and professional boundaries
respond respectfully and promptly when a staff member requests a meeting about a student’s learning, behaviour, attendance, safety or wellbeing
avoid raising complex, sensitive or confidential matters during arrival, dismissal, public events or times when staff are supervising students
allow staff reasonable time to consider and respond to communications
Parents and guardians must not:
contact staff at their home or through personal social media accounts
pressure staff to respond outside reasonable working expectations
record staff conversations or meetings without consent
confront staff in public or in the presence of students
attempt to direct staff in the performance of their duties
Child safety and student wellbeing
Parents and guardians must support the College’s child-safe culture.
Parents and guardians must:
comply with child safety, visitor, supervision and offsite activity requirements
avoid unsupervised contact with students unless authorised by the College
report child safety or wellbeing concerns promptly to the Principal or another appropriate staff member
respect boundaries with students, including online and physical boundaries
avoid photographing, recording or sharing images of students except where permitted by the College
follow staff directions during emergencies, evacuations, lockdowns, first aid incidents or safety concerns
respect student privacy and supervision boundaries around the Toilet Building, First Aid Room, classrooms, student movement routes and supervised play areas
Concerns involving child safety, mandatory reporting, reportable conduct, criminal conduct or immediate risk must be escalated under the relevant College procedure and must not be treated only as a general complaint.
Student needs, family circumstances and risk information
Parents and guardians must provide the College with accurate and current information needed to support student learning, safety and wellbeing.
Parents and guardians are expected to inform the College as soon as practicable about:
medical, health, allergy, medication, disability or wellbeing needs
behavioural, educational, personal or family circumstances that may affect the student at school
changes to emergency contacts, authorised collection arrangements or court orders
incidents outside school, including online conduct, that may affect the safety, wellbeing or learning of any student
any concern that a student may be unsafe, distressed, bullied, excluded, harmed or at risk
The College uses this information to assess risk, provide support, meet legal obligations and maintain a safe environment for students, staff and families.
Respect for staff roles and professional judgement
Parents and guardians are expected to respect the professional role of staff and the operational authority of the Principal.
Parents and guardians may raise concerns, ask questions and request clarification, but must not:
direct staff in the performance of their duties
discipline or question another person’s child
approach another student about a behaviour, conflict or complaint matter
interfere with supervision, teaching, emergency response or behaviour management
seek confidential information about another student, family or staff member
pressure staff to act outside policy, procedure or professional judgement
undermine the authority of staff in front of students or other members of the College community
The College is responsible for assessing behaviour matters and determining appropriate responses in accordance with its policies and procedures. Parents and guardians may raise concerns through the Complaints and Grievances Policy and Procedure, but must not undermine staff authority, interfere with investigations or attempt to resolve student behaviour matters directly with other students or families.
Arrival, dismissal and movement through the site
Parents and guardians must follow College arrangements for arrival, dismissal, late arrival, early collection and visitor access.
Parents and guardians are expected to:
use the approved student and visitor entry arrangements
report to Reception when required
follow staff directions during arrival, dismissal, early collection, events, emergencies and changes to ordinary access arrangements
remain in parent, visitor or event areas unless authorised to enter another area
avoid entering classrooms, staff areas, administration areas, the Northern Service Yard, Southern Service Yard, storage areas, contractor areas or student toilet areas unless authorised by staff
supervise younger siblings or accompanying children while onsite
avoid blocking gates, paths, ramps, stairs, emergency access, service access or supervised student movement routes
leave promptly when requested by staff for safety, supervision or operational reasons
Parents and guardians must not approach a student other than their own child about a behaviour, conflict, complaint or supervision matter. Concerns about another student must be raised with staff.
Student collection and handover
Parents and guardians must comply with the College’s student collection and handover arrangements.
Parents and guardians are expected to:
ensure the College has current parent, guardian and emergency contact details
ensure authorised collection information is accurate and current
notify the College of absences, late arrivals and early collections in accordance with College procedures
report to Reception for late arrival and early collection where required
wait for staff to release a student before taking the student from College supervision
follow staff instructions if a collection arrangement is unclear, changed or cannot be verified
avoid calling students away from supervised areas without staff knowledge and approval
follow emergency collection or reunification instructions if ordinary collection arrangements change
The College does not release a student where collection authority is uncertain or where release would create a foreseeable safety risk.
Separated parents and family disputes
The College seeks to maintain appropriate communication with parents and guardians in accordance with enrolment records, legal obligations and any court orders or formal parenting arrangements provided to the College.
Parents and guardians must not ask the College to take sides in parental, family or relationship disputes.
Parents and guardians are expected to:
provide the College with current court orders or formal arrangements relevant to student safety, communication, access or collection
avoid using College staff, records, events, communication systems or student collection arrangements to pursue a family dispute
communicate with the College respectfully and factually about matters affecting the student
understand that the College complies with applicable legal obligations and acts in the student’s best interests and safety
Raising concerns and complaints
The College welcomes concerns raised in good faith through appropriate channels.
Parents and guardians are expected to:
raise concerns early and respectfully
use the Complaints and Grievances Policy and Procedure where a matter requires formal resolution
allow the College reasonable time to assess and respond
provide accurate information
respect confidentiality and procedural fairness
avoid escalating concerns through gossip, social media or inappropriate community pressure
Raising a complaint in good faith will not disadvantage a student or family. However, complaint rights do not permit threatening, abusive, unsafe, defamatory, unreasonable or public conduct that undermines the safety, dignity or reputation of staff, students, families or the College.
Parents and guardians must not use gossip, speculation, social media, class groups or community pressure as a substitute for the College’s complaints process.
Where a matter involves another student, another family, child safety, behaviour management, bullying, an investigation or a confidential College process, parents and guardians must raise the matter with the College and must not approach another student, parent or family without College knowledge and consent.
Attendance, punctuality and student responsibilities
Parents and guardians support student conduct and learning by:
ensuring students attend school regularly and punctually
notifying the College of absences in accordance with attendance procedures
supporting uniform, presentation, technology and behaviour expectations
providing accurate health, medical, wellbeing and contact information
working with staff where a student requires additional support
supporting agreed student management, wellbeing or learning plans
Privacy and confidentiality
Parents and guardians must respect the privacy and dignity of others.
Parents and guardians must not:
share confidential information about students, families, staff or College matters without authority
record meetings, conversations, classes, events or incidents without permission
publish images or information about other students without appropriate consent
misuse parent contact details, class information or College communications
seek access to records or information to which they are not entitled
photograph or record students in toilets, first aid areas, classrooms, supervised play areas or other sensitive spaces
Technology, social media and parent communication groups
Parents and guardians must use technology, social media and parent communication groups responsibly.
Parents and guardians must not:
use social media, messaging groups, email or online forums to bully, harass, shame, defame or undermine staff, students, parents, families or the College
publish confidential, sensitive or personal information about staff, students, parents or College matters without authority
publish images, recordings or personal information about students other than their own child without appropriate consent
publish images or recordings that show inappropriate behaviour by students, staff, parents or community members connected with the College
discuss grievances about individual staff, students or families online
use the College’s name, logo, insignia or identity for an online group, publication, forum or communication channel in a way that suggests College endorsement without written approval
contact staff through personal social media accounts or personal online platforms about College matters
Concerns about online behaviour, images, recordings, messaging groups or digital communication that affect student safety or wellbeing must be raised with the College.
Use of College grounds and events
Parents and guardians must comply with College directions regarding:
signing in and visitor access
supervision zones and restricted areas
arrival, dismissal, pedestrian access and student handover arrangements
emergency and evacuation procedures
student collection and authorised contacts
event attendance and conduct
site-specific safety requirements
Parents and guardians must not enter restricted or controlled areas unless authorised by staff.
Restricted or controlled areas may include:
staff work areas
administration work areas, including the Office and Principal’s Office
student toilet areas
the First Aid Room, except where invited by staff
the Northern Service Yard and Southern Service Yard
utility or plant areas
contractor work zones
storage areas
unattended buildings
emergency access and service access areas
Parents and guardians attending College events must:
model respectful conduct for students
follow the directions of staff, event supervisors, coaches, officials and authorised College representatives
avoid abusive, threatening, intimidating or undermining behaviour toward staff, volunteers, officials, students, parents or visitors
accept that staff make decisions about student participation, grouping, selection and supervision in accordance with College responsibilities and professional judgement
Volunteering and parent participation
Parents and guardians who volunteer or participate in College activities must comply with all applicable screening, induction, child safety, supervision, privacy and staff direction requirements.
Volunteering or parent participation does not give a parent or guardian authority to:
supervise students independently unless authorised by the College
access confidential information
discipline students
direct staff or students outside the role approved by the College
enter restricted areas without authorisation
take photographs, videos or recordings except where authorised
use volunteer access to advance a personal complaint or family dispute
Managing breaches of this policy
Where a parent or guardian breaches this policy, the College may take action that is reasonable, proportionate and directed to safety, respectful communication and the continued education of the student.
Possible responses include:
reminder of expectations
request to communicate through a nominated staff member
meeting with the Principal
written warning
limits on access to a staff member or group of staff members
requirement that communication occur only in writing or only through a nominated staff member
limits on access to College grounds or events
revised communication arrangements
requirement to report to Reception before entering College areas
exclusion from volunteering or specific activities
suspension from attendance at functions, activities or events for a specified period
requirement to attend a meeting before further attendance onsite or at events
direction to leave the site
removal from, or refusal of participation in, parent communication groups, volunteering or informal activities connected with the College
escalation under child safety, complaints, emergency, privacy or legal procedures
referral to external authorities where required
consideration of enrolment implications where conduct seriously undermines safety, trust or the College’s ability to educate the student
Any action must take into account student welfare, procedural fairness, child safety, duty of care, disability and vulnerability considerations, and the seriousness and context of the conduct.
Implementation
The Principal is responsible for implementing this policy.
The Principal is responsible for:
communicating this policy to parents and guardians
ensuring staff know how to respond to parent conduct concerns
managing serious or repeated conduct concerns
ensuring child safety matters are escalated appropriately
maintaining records of significant parent conduct issues
reporting significant risks, incidents or patterns to the Governing Authority where appropriate
ensuring arrival, dismissal, visitor access and collection expectations are reflected in parent communication
ensuring parent partnership expectations are reflected in the Parent Handbook, enrolment communication and induction processes
Staff are responsible for:
modelling respectful communication
maintaining professional boundaries
applying visitor, arrival, dismissal and student collection arrangements
referring serious or repeated concerns to the Principal
recording relevant parent conduct concerns in approved College systems
following child safety, complaints, privacy and incident procedures where applicable
using approved College communication channels when communicating with parents and guardians
Parents and guardians are responsible for:
reading and following this policy
supporting respectful partnership between home and the College
raising concerns through appropriate channels
complying with staff directions while onsite or participating in College activities
ensuring other family members attending College activities understand and follow relevant conduct expectations
keeping student, family, medical, contact, collection and court order information accurate and current
supporting the College’s behaviour, attendance, uniform, technology and safety expectations
Records are maintained in accordance with the College’s privacy, complaints, incident and records management requirements.
Review
This policy will be reviewed at least every three years, or earlier if required due to:
a serious parent conduct, child safety, complaints or safety incident
changes to legislation, Ministerial Orders, VRQA guidance or registration expectations
changes to the College’s buildings, access points, student access boundaries, Site Supervision Map, supervision, student collection or operational arrangements
changes to related College policies or procedures
feedback from staff, parents, guardians or the Governing Authority
a governance or operational review identifying that the policy is unclear, incomplete or ineffective
The Principal is responsible for coordinating review.
Material amendments must be approved by the Governing Authority.
Related Documents
Related documents include:

Enrolment Agreement
Parent Handbook

## Student Code of Conduct Policy

Purpose
The purpose of this policy is to set out the conduct expected of students at Rosewood College.
Rosewood College (the College) is an independent school teaching the Catholic faith. The College seeks to form students in faith, virtue, responsibility and respect, and to provide a safe, orderly and caring learning environment where each student is known, valued and supported to grow.
This policy supports student safety, wellbeing, learning, behaviour formation, child safety, duty of care, respectful relationships, anti-bullying practice and the College’s commitment to Australian democratic principles.
This policy recognises that Rosewood College students are primary-aged students from Foundation to Year 5. Student expectations are therefore taught, modelled, practised and reinforced in an age-appropriate way, with staff support and parent partnership.
Scope
This policy applies to all students of Rosewood College.
It applies whenever a student is participating in, representing or identifiable as connected with the College, including:
during the school day
before and after school while under College supervision
during class, break times, assemblies, liturgies, Mass, formation activities and College events
during excursions, sport, performances and offsite activities, including camps where approved by the College
during online learning or digital communication connected with the College
while travelling to or from school where behaviour affects the safety, wellbeing or reputation of the College community
during interactions with students, staff, parents, volunteers, contractors, visitors and members of the wider community
Policy
Student conduct principles
Students are expected to conduct themselves in a manner consistent with the College’s Catholic identity, philosophy, values and commitment to the dignity of every person.
Students are expected to:
act with respect, honesty and kindness
listen to staff and follow reasonable staff directions
try their best in learning and College activities
use safe hands, safe feet and respectful words
care for younger students and be a good example to others
treat others fairly and include others where possible
respect the property, privacy and personal space of others
wear the College uniform correctly and with care
use technology only as allowed by staff
ask a staff member for help when they feel worried, unsafe, hurt, confused or unsure what to do
Students are learning how to make good choices. Staff support students to understand expectations, practise respectful behaviour, repair harm where appropriate and seek help when they need it.
Respect for others
Students must treat every person with dignity and respect.
Students are expected to:
speak kindly and truthfully
listen when others are speaking
take turns and share fairly
keep hands, feet and objects to themselves
respect differences between people
include others and avoid leaving people out on purpose
say sorry and repair harm where appropriate
tell a staff member if someone is being hurt, bullied, excluded or treated unfairly
Students must not:
bully, tease, threaten, intimidate or humiliate others
use words, gestures, drawings, images or actions that are rude, cruel, racist, sexist, discriminatory or degrading
hurt another person physically
damage another person’s belongings
spread rumours or private information
encourage others to do the wrong thing
pressure another student to keep unsafe behaviour secret
respond to conflict with aggression or revenge
Safety and child safety
Students must act in ways that support their own safety and the safety of others.
Students are expected to:
tell a staff member if they or another student feel unsafe
report bullying, harassment, unsafe behaviour or child safety concerns
follow staff instructions during supervision, first aid, emergencies and offsite activities
stay in approved student areas
use equipment, furniture, resources and facilities safely
avoid bringing unsafe, prohibited or inappropriate items to school
seek adult help rather than trying to manage serious problems alone
Students must not:
leave the College boundary without permission and authorised collection
hide from staff supervision
climb on fences, gates, buildings, roofs, ramps, stairs, furniture or equipment not intended for climbing
interfere with emergency equipment, first aid equipment, gates, locks, signs or safety controls
touch hazardous materials, cleaning products, maintenance equipment, tools or contractor equipment
enter staff-only areas, service areas, utility areas, contractor areas or restricted areas unless authorised and supervised
Child safety concerns must always be treated as safety matters first. Behaviour that may involve child abuse, grooming, sexual misconduct, reportable conduct, mandatory reporting, criminal conduct or serious risk must be escalated under the College’s child safety and incident management procedures.
Movement, buildings and play areas
Students are expected to move safely and calmly around the College.
Students must:
stay in areas approved for student use
move between the Classroom Building, Administration Building, Covered Deck, Toilet Building, Covered Play Area and Playground and Open Play Area as directed by staff
walk on decks, ramps, stairs, paths and indoor areas
stay with their class or group unless a staff member gives permission to leave
ask a staff member before going to Reception, the First Aid Room, the Chapel / Multi-Purpose Space or the Interview Room
keep away from the Northern Service Yard, Southern Service Yard, utility areas, plant areas, contractor areas, storage areas, staff areas and unattended buildings unless a staff member gives permission and supervises the access
tell a staff member if a gate, fence, path, ramp, stair, toilet area, playground area or building area looks unsafe
Students must not:
enter restricted or no-play areas
cross service or emergency access areas unless supervised by staff
remain in an activity space after the responsible staff member has left
run indoors, on decks, on ramps, on stairs or in transition areas
play in areas that staff have closed, restricted or identified as unsafe
interfere with deliveries, maintenance, service access or emergency access
Toilets and privacy
Students must use the Toilet Building safely, respectfully and only for its proper purpose.
Students are expected to:
go to the Toilet Building with staff permission or in accordance with class routines
return promptly to the supervised area
respect the privacy of others
use quiet and appropriate behaviour
wash hands before returning to learning or play
tell a staff member if they feel unsafe
tell a staff member if another person does not respect privacy in or near the Toilet Building
tell a staff member if another student is unwell, upset, hurt or unsafe
tell a staff member if the toilets need cleaning or maintenance
Students must not:
play, hide, climb, damage property or waste supplies in or near the Toilet Building
look into private spaces
block doors or prevent another student from leaving
tease, frighten, shame or exclude others
use the Toilet Building as a place to avoid class, supervision or staff directions
enter a toilet area not allocated for their use unless a staff member has authorised an individual arrangement
Learning and participation
Students are expected to:
attend school and classes punctually
come prepared for learning
listen respectfully to teachers and other students
allow others to learn without disruption
try their best and complete learning tasks
participate in prayer, formation, assemblies, liturgies, Mass where celebrated, and College activities with respect
accept feedback and correction respectfully
ask for help when learning, wellbeing or behaviour difficulties arise
Students are not expected to solve every difficulty on their own. Students should ask a staff member for help when they do not understand work, feel upset, experience conflict or are unsure what choice to make.
Property and the College environment
Students are expected to:
care for College property, resources, books, technology, equipment and facilities
respect the belongings of others
keep classrooms, outdoor areas, toilets and shared spaces clean and orderly
put rubbish in bins
use furniture and equipment for their intended purpose
report damage, hazards or unsafe conditions to staff
avoid vandalism, theft, misuse or waste of property
Technology and online conduct
Students must use technology in accordance with the College’s Internet and Technology Use Policy and staff instructions.
Students must:
use devices only when allowed by staff
use College systems and accounts appropriately
keep passwords and login details private
be kind and respectful in online communication
tell a staff member if they see unsafe, upsetting or inappropriate online content
tell a staff member if technology is being used to hurt, embarrass, threaten or exclude someone
Students must not:
use technology to bully, harass, threaten, shame or exclude others
record, photograph or share images of others without permission
access, create or share inappropriate, harmful or unsafe content
pretend to be another person online
misuse passwords, accounts or systems
interfere with College systems or digital learning environments
use personal devices contrary to College expectations
Conduct outside the classroom
Students are expected to uphold this policy during:
recess and lunch
arrival and dismissal
transitions between learning areas
assemblies, prayer, liturgies and Mass
visits to Reception or the First Aid Room
use of the Toilet Building
wet-weather arrangements
excursions, camps and offsite activities
sport, performances and community events
online interactions connected with the College
Response to student conduct concerns
The College responds to student conduct concerns in a manner that is:
child-safe
age-appropriate
fair and consistent
educative and restorative where appropriate
proportionate to the seriousness and context of the behaviour
attentive to disability, vulnerability, trauma, health, wellbeing and developmental factors
consistent with duty of care, supervision and behaviour management obligations
Possible responses may include:
reminder or redirection
re-teaching the expected behaviour
moving a student to a safer or more suitable place
restorative conversation
apology or repair of harm where appropriate
loss of access to an activity or area for a period of time
parent or guardian contact
mentoring or wellbeing support
behaviour support strategies
adjustment to supervision or participation arrangements
recording in behaviour or incident records
formal behaviour management action
suspension or expulsion only in accordance with the Suspension and Expulsion Procedure
Corporal punishment is prohibited.
Implementation
The Principal is responsible for implementing this policy.
Staff are responsible for:
modelling respectful, safe and child-safe conduct
teaching student expectations in age-appropriate language
using routines, reminders, visual supports and explicit instruction where helpful
supervising students actively in accordance with College supervision arrangements
reinforcing safe movement, toilet, playground, classroom and technology expectations
responding to conduct concerns promptly
recording behaviour, safety or wellbeing concerns as required
escalating serious concerns in accordance with College procedures
applying behaviour responses fairly and consistently
Students are responsible for:
learning and following this policy at an age-appropriate level
asking for help when needed
listening to staff direction and correction
helping to keep the College safe and welcoming
repairing harm where appropriate
Parents and guardians support implementation by:
reinforcing College expectations at home
encouraging students to seek staff help when needed
working respectfully with staff
supporting behaviour, wellbeing or learning plans where required
raising concerns through appropriate College channels
The College communicates student expectations through age-appropriate classroom routines, staff direction, parent communication, the Parent Handbook, induction processes and related policies and procedures.
Records relating to student conduct are managed in accordance with the College’s behaviour, incident, complaints, privacy and records management procedures.
Review
This policy will be reviewed at least every two years, or earlier if required due to:
a serious student conduct, child safety or wellbeing incident
changes to legislation, Ministerial Orders, VRQA guidance or registration expectations
changes to the College’s buildings, student access boundaries, supervision model, student cohort or operational arrangements
changes to related College policies or procedures
feedback from staff, students, parents or guardians
a governance or operational review identifying that the policy is unclear, incomplete or ineffective
The Principal is responsible for coordinating review.
Material amendments must be approved by the Governing Authority.
Related Documents
Related documents include:

Child Safety Code of Conduct Policy
Internet and Technology Use Policy
Student Behaviour Management Policy
Uniform Policy

## Child Safety Code of Conduct Policy

Exported on 30 Jun 2026
Purpose
The purpose of this Policy is to establish clear behavioural expectations that promote and support a child-safe culture at Rosewood College.
This Policy sets standards of conduct for adults interacting with children and ensures that all interactions with students are safe, respectful, professional and consistent with the College's commitment to child safety and wellbeing.
As an independent school grounded in the Catholic faith and moral tradition, Rosewood College recognises that all adults share responsibility for protecting children from abuse, harm, neglect, exploitation, grooming and other inappropriate conduct.
This Policy supports the Child Safe Standards framework and applies in conjunction with the Child Safety Policy and other child safety governance documents.
Scope
This Policy applies to:
members of the Governing Authority
the Principal
all staff
volunteers
contractors
trainee teachers
work experience participants
external providers
visitors
any person engaged in child-connected work on behalf of the College
This Policy applies whenever a person is:
on College premises
participating in College activities
supervising students
representing the College
communicating with students
interacting with students online
undertaking work on behalf of the College
This Policy applies to conduct connected with Rosewood College, including conduct that occurs on College premises, during school activities, during excursions or offsite activities, online, through digital communication, outside school hours, away from College premises, or in any other context where the conduct involves a student, affects student safety or wellbeing, relates to a school-authorised activity, or may affect trust and confidence in the College’s child safety arrangements.
Policy
Child Safety Commitment
All adults associated with Rosewood College must contribute to a culture in which:
the safety, wellbeing and best interests of children are paramount
children are treated with dignity and respect
students feel safe to raise concerns
safeguarding responsibilities are understood and fulfilled
concerns are reported promptly
professional boundaries are maintained
Required Standards of Conduct
All persons covered by this Policy must:
act in the best interests of students
treat students with respect, fairness and dignity
promote inclusion and participation
model respectful behaviour
maintain appropriate professional boundaries
comply with child safety obligations
comply with all College policies and procedures
report child safety concerns promptly
take reasonable steps to protect students from foreseeable harm
support a child-safe environment
intervene or seek assistance when witnessing behaviour that may place a child at risk
report actual or suspected breaches of this Policy
Professional Boundaries
Adults must maintain clear professional boundaries with students at all times.
Professional interactions must:
be appropriate to the person's role
support the student's educational, wellbeing or safety needs
be transparent and capable of scrutiny
occur within approved College arrangements
Adults must avoid relationships with students that may:
create favouritism
create dependency
undermine professional judgement
compromise child safety
place either the student or adult at risk
Adults must discourage, reject and report any inappropriate emotional, romantic or sexual attention initiated by a student.
Any actual, potential or perceived conflict of interest affecting an adult’s professional relationship with a student must be disclosed to the Principal as soon as practicable.
Acceptable Conduct
Examples of acceptable conduct include:
listening respectfully to students
encouraging student participation and inclusion
maintaining appropriate supervision
providing educational guidance and support
responding appropriately to student wellbeing concerns
following approved communication protocols
using positive behaviour management practices
supporting students to understand their rights and responsibilities
respecting each student’s dignity, background, family circumstances, faith, culture and individual needs
Unacceptable Conduct
Persons covered by this Policy must not:
engage in any form of child abuse
groom a child or young person
engage in sexual conduct with a child
engage in sexualised behaviour towards a child
use physical punishment
humiliate, ridicule or shame a student
engage in conduct that demeans, excludes or unfairly targets a student because of their background, circumstances, characteristics or needs
ignore or dismiss child safety concerns
expose students to inappropriate material
develop inappropriate personal relationships with students
use inappropriate language towards students
deliberately intimidate, threaten or coerce a student
engage in conduct that places a child at risk of harm
Physical Contact
Physical contact with students must:
be reasonable
be necessary in the circumstances
be appropriate to the student's age and developmental needs
be responsive to the student's safety, wellbeing or educational needs
take place in a manner that is observable and accountable
Examples of circumstances where physical contact may be appropriate include:
providing first aid
protecting a student from immediate harm
assisting with mobility or disability support
participating in approved educational or sporting activities where contact is unavoidable
Physical contact must never be:
sexualised
secretive
intimidating
unnecessary
motivated by personal needs
One-to-One Interactions
One-to-one interactions with students must occur in circumstances that support transparency and accountability.
Adults must not conduct undisclosed, unauthorised or unnecessary private meetings with students.
Where practicable:
interactions must occur in observable locations
another adult must be aware of the interaction
visibility must be maintained
unnecessary isolation must be avoided
The College recognises that some educational, wellbeing, counselling or support activities may require individual meetings with students.
Appropriate safeguards must be maintained.
Electronic Communication and Online Conduct
Communication with students must:
support legitimate educational, wellbeing or operational purposes
occur through approved College communication channels wherever practicable
be professional and respectful
be capable of review where required
Adults must not:
communicate with students through personal social media accounts
establish social media relationships with students
use personal messaging applications to communicate with students unless expressly authorised by the Principal for a legitimate College purpose and subject to safeguards
engage in private or secretive electronic communications with students
use electronic communication in a way that circumvents College oversight or recordkeeping
Transporting Students
Staff and other authorised persons must comply with College requirements regarding student transport.
Transport arrangements must:
be authorised
be documented where required
prioritise student safety
comply with supervision and risk management requirements
Unauthorised transport arrangements are prohibited.
Photography, Video and Images
Images, recordings and photographs of students may only be created, stored, used or shared:
for authorised College purposes
in accordance with College policies
in accordance with applicable consent requirements
in accordance with privacy obligations
Adults must not use personal devices or images in ways that compromise child safety or privacy.
Gifts, Favouritism and Personal Relationships
Adults must not:
provide gifts that could create inappropriate influence or dependency
show favouritism towards particular students
seek emotional support from students
develop relationships that blur professional boundaries
Professional judgement must always be maintained.
Reporting Obligations
All persons covered by this Policy must:
report child safety concerns promptly
comply with mandatory reporting obligations where applicable
comply with reportable conduct requirements
cooperate with child safety investigations
support safeguarding actions
create or contribute to required records relating to child safety concerns, disclosures, incidents or breaches
Failure to report concerns may place children at risk and may breach legal or professional obligations.
Breaches of This Policy
Actual or suspected breaches of this Policy will be taken seriously.
Breaches may result in:
performance management action
disciplinary action
removal from duties
termination of engagement
reporting to relevant authorities
regulatory notification
other action considered necessary to protect children
Implementation
The Governing Authority is responsible for approving this Policy and maintaining oversight of child safety governance.
The Governing Authority is responsible for approving, endorsing and ensuring this Policy is made publicly available to students, parents, guardians, staff, volunteers and the school community through the College website or another approved access point.
The Principal is responsible for:
implementing this Policy
communicating behavioural expectations
ensuring induction and training occurs
monitoring compliance
responding to breaches
supporting a child-safe culture
All staff, volunteers, contractors and external providers are responsible for:
complying with this Policy
maintaining professional boundaries
reporting concerns promptly
participating in child safety training
modelling appropriate conduct
The College ensures this Policy is communicated during recruitment, induction and periodic refresher training. Persons undertaking child-connected work must be informed of this Policy and must confirm that they understand and agree to comply with it before commencing relevant duties, unless the Principal approves an alternative documented arrangement due to urgent or exceptional circumstances.
Review
This Policy will be reviewed at least every two years, and earlier where required due to a child safety incident, reportable conduct matter, complaint, legislative change, regulatory update, audit finding, training review, identified breach pattern, safeguarding improvement, or change to Child Safe Standards requirements.
The review must consider whether the Policy remains clear, current, understood and effective in guiding safe adult behaviour with students.
The Principal is responsible for coordinating review.
Material amendments must be approved by the Governing Authority.

Staff Code of Conduct
Student Code of Conduct Policy

## ICT Acceptable Use Agreement

Purpose
The purpose of this ICT Acceptable Use Agreement is to set out the expectations that apply when students use internet access, digital technology, online platforms, College systems, student accounts and devices connected with Rosewood College.
Rosewood College (the College) provides or authorises technology to support learning, communication, creativity, research, curriculum delivery and safe participation in College life.
The College expects technology to be used in a way that is safe, respectful, lawful, age-appropriate, supervised and consistent with the College’s Catholic identity, moral tradition, child safety obligations and educational purpose.
This Agreement supports the Internet and Technology Use Policy and must be read together with that policy.
Scope
This Agreement applies to students and parents or guardians.
It applies to student use of:
College internet access
College-owned devices
College-approved software, applications and online platforms
student accounts created or authorised by the College
email, messaging or communication systems approved by the College
online learning environments
assistive technology or approved learning support tools
personal devices where the College has authorised their use
digital communication connected with College learning or College activities
This Agreement applies during:
onsite learning
supervised technology use
specialist learning activities
NAPLAN or other approved assessments
excursions, incursions or offsite activities where technology is authorised
remote or online learning where approved by the College
any digital conduct that affects student safety, wellbeing, learning or participation at the College
Meaning of ICT and devices
In this Agreement, ICT and devices include:
internet-based services, software, applications and online platforms
computers, laptops, tablets and other internet-enabled devices
cameras and recording devices
mobile phones and smartphones
smart watches, fitness trackers and other wearable devices that can send, receive, record or store information
gaming devices
Bluetooth-enabled or SIM-enabled devices
any other device or system that can access the internet, store information, communicate with another device, record images or audio, or connect to a wired or wireless network
Agreement principles
Technology use at the College is guided by the following principles:
technology is used for approved educational and College-related purposes
students use technology under staff direction and supervision
students are taught age-appropriate digital safety and responsibility
students treat others with dignity and respect online and offline
student privacy, child safety and personal information are protected
parents and guardians support safe and responsible technology use
unsafe, harmful or inappropriate technology use is reported and addressed
technology supports learning and formation, and does not replace direct teaching, personal responsibility or respectful human relationships
Student responsibilities
Students must use ICT and devices safely, respectfully and only as allowed by staff.
Students must:
ask a staff member before using College technology or internet access
use technology only for the task or activity approved by staff
follow staff instructions about when, where and how technology may be used
use kind, respectful and appropriate words online
keep passwords and login details private
use only their own account unless a staff member gives permission
take care of College devices and equipment
tell a staff member if a device, screen, message, website, image or video makes them feel worried, unsafe or uncomfortable
tell a staff member if someone uses technology to hurt, frighten, embarrass, exclude or threaten another person
log out, close devices or return equipment when directed by staff
use technology in a way that supports learning and respects others
Students must not:
use technology without staff permission
use technology to bully, tease, shame, threaten, frighten or exclude another person
search for, open, create, send or share inappropriate, violent, sexual, discriminatory, offensive or unsafe content
photograph, video, livestream or record another person unless a staff member gives permission and appropriate consent is in place
share private information about themselves or another person
share their password or use another person’s password
access another person’s account, files, messages or work without permission
pretend to be another person online
contact unknown people through College technology
contact staff through unauthorised digital channels
use social media, gaming, chat platforms or personal messaging during College activities unless expressly authorised by staff
install, download or use unauthorised software, games, applications, extensions or files
change settings, bypass filters or interfere with College systems
damage, hide, remove, misuse or tamper with College devices or equipment
use artificial intelligence tools unless a staff member has authorised their use for the learning task
use technology to cheat, copy work or pretend that someone else’s work is their own
Personal devices
Students are not permitted to use personal devices during College hours or College activities unless authorised by the Principal or supervising staff.
Personal devices include:
mobile phones
smart watches
tablets
laptops
cameras
gaming devices
Bluetooth-enabled devices
SIM-enabled devices
devices capable of internet access, messaging, recording, image capture or data storage
Where a personal device is authorised, the student must use it only in accordance with staff directions.
Students must not:
connect a personal device to the College network unless authorised
use a personal hotspot at the College
access or request the College Wi-Fi password
use a staff member’s personal device
use another student’s device without permission and staff approval
use a personal device to record, photograph, message, call, livestream or access online content during College activities unless authorised
The College may require a student to hand a personal device to staff for safe storage where required for student safety, privacy, learning, supervision or compliance with College expectations.
College accounts, email and approved platforms
Where the College provides a student account, email account or approved platform access, the account remains a College-controlled account.
Student accounts may be used for:
accessing approved learning platforms
completing learning activities
saving and submitting College work
receiving teacher feedback
communicating with staff for approved learning purposes
approved collaboration on schoolwork
accessing assistive technology or learning support tools
participating in supervised online learning activities
Student accounts must not be used for:
personal messaging unrelated to College learning
social media or gaming accounts
registering for personal applications, games or services
communicating with unknown people
sending inappropriate messages or content
sharing files, images, audio or video unrelated to approved College learning
storing personal, offensive, unsafe or inappropriate material
bypassing College systems, filters or monitoring arrangements
The College may access, review, suspend or close student accounts where necessary for safety, wellbeing, supervision, investigation, privacy, security, records management or operational reasons.
Cyber safety and online harm
Students have the right to learn in a safe environment, including when using technology.
Cyber safety concerns may include:
cyberbullying
online harassment
unsafe adult contact
grooming or predatory behaviour
image-based abuse
inappropriate messages or content
impersonation
spreading rumours online
excluding someone from an online group in a harmful way
sharing private information without permission
repeated unwanted digital contact
accessing harmful or age-inappropriate material
unsafe gaming, chat or social media interactions
Students must report cyber safety concerns to a staff member as soon as possible.
Parents and guardians are encouraged to report cyber safety concerns to the College where the concern may affect student safety, wellbeing, learning or participation at the College.
Online child safety concerns must not be treated only as technology breaches where student safety, abuse, grooming, exploitation, serious harm or adult misconduct may be involved.
Social media, messaging and online groups
Students must not use social media, personal messaging, gaming chat or online group chat during College hours or College activities unless expressly authorised and supervised by staff for a College purpose.
Students must not use College systems or devices to:
access social media
create social media accounts
communicate with unknown people
join unauthorised online groups
share images or recordings of students or staff
post comments about students, staff, families or the College
participate in online conduct that is unsafe, unkind, disrespectful or harmful
Staff communication with students occurs through approved College channels and in accordance with child safety and professional conduct requirements.
Parents and guardians are asked not to encourage students to contact staff through personal social media accounts or unauthorised communication platforms.
Photography, recording and image sharing
Students must not photograph, video, livestream, record or share images, audio or video of another person unless:
staff have authorised the activity
the activity has a legitimate College purpose
appropriate permission or consent is in place
the recording or image is used only for the approved purpose
privacy, dignity and child safety requirements are respected
Students must never photograph, video, livestream or record in the Toilet Building, the First Aid Room, change areas, private spaces or any other sensitive location.
Unauthorised photography, recording or sharing may be treated as a serious breach, especially where it involves humiliation, bullying, harassment, violence, sexualised content, privacy breach or child safety concern.
Privacy and personal information
Students must protect their own personal information and the personal information of others.
Students must not share:
full names
addresses
phone numbers
dates of birth
passwords
account details
images or recordings
location information
family information
medical or wellbeing information
private messages
College records
student work that is not intended for sharing
Staff guide students to understand safe information sharing according to their age, maturity and learning context.
Artificial intelligence and digital tools
Students may use artificial intelligence tools only when authorised by staff and only for the approved learning purpose.
Students must not use artificial intelligence or digital tools to:
pretend that generated work is their own
avoid doing required learning
create or share harmful, false, misleading or inappropriate content
create images, recordings or material that embarrasses, harms or humiliates another person
upload personal, sensitive, confidential or College information without authorisation
breach privacy, copyright or assessment expectations
Staff provide clear instructions when artificial intelligence or digital tools may or may not be used.
Parent and guardian responsibilities
Parents and guardians support safe and responsible ICT use by:
reading this Agreement with their child in an age-appropriate way
helping their child understand College technology expectations
reinforcing respectful and safe online conduct at home
supporting the College’s restrictions on personal devices
monitoring student use of personal devices and accounts outside school where relevant
reporting cyberbullying, online harm, unsafe contact or inappropriate digital conduct that may affect student safety, wellbeing, learning or participation at the College
ensuring student use of personal devices or personal accounts does not compromise College safety, learning, privacy or wellbeing
working constructively with the College where concerns arise
ensuring any device brought to the College for an approved reason is clearly identified and used only as authorised
Parents and guardians are encouraged to:
keep technology use visible and supervised at home
set device-free times and places
delay access to personal internet-enabled devices where possible
use age-appropriate content and parental controls
talk with children about online safety, kindness, privacy and help-seeking
avoid posting images of other students without appropriate permission
contact the College promptly if online conduct creates a concern for student safety or wellbeing
Staff responsibilities
Staff support safe and appropriate student ICT use by:
modelling responsible technology use
using approved College systems for school-related communication and records
giving clear instructions about permitted technology use
supervising or monitoring student technology use according to the activity and risk
selecting age-appropriate digital learning activities
protecting student privacy and personal information
responding promptly to unsafe or inappropriate use
reporting cyber safety, online harm, child safety, privacy, security or technology misuse concerns
maintaining professional boundaries in digital communication
avoiding personal accounts or unauthorised channels for student communication
Staff must not ignore online conduct that creates a foreseeable risk to student safety or wellbeing.
Breaches of this Agreement
A breach of this Agreement may result in action proportionate to the seriousness of the conduct.
Possible responses include:
reminder or redirection
re-teaching expected behaviour
temporary restriction of device, internet or platform access
removal of access to a device or system for a period of time
parent or guardian communication
behaviour support
incident recording
anti-bullying or harassment response
child safety escalation
privacy or data breach response
complaint handling
referral to external authorities where required
action under the Student Behaviour Management Policy or related procedures
The College’s response considers the student’s age, maturity, intent, impact, vulnerability, prior conduct and the seriousness of the risk.
Records
The College maintains records where ICT use gives rise to a safety, wellbeing, behaviour, child safety, privacy, incident, complaint, disciplinary or security concern.
Records may include:
student or parent acknowledgement of this Agreement
behaviour records

cyberbullying records

staff briefing or training records
Records are managed in accordance with the Records Management Policy and Privacy Policy.
Review
This Agreement is reviewed at least every three years, or earlier if required due to:
a serious cyberbullying, online harm, privacy, child safety or technology misuse incident

The Principal is responsible for coordinating review.
