## Student Behaviour Management Policy

Exported on 30 Jun 2026
Purpose
The purpose of this Policy is to establish the principles and expectations for student behaviour at Rosewood College, and to articulate the College’s approach to behaviour management in a manner consistent with its educational philosophy and regulatory obligations.
This Policy provides the framework through which the College promotes positive student behaviour, supports the formation of character, and maintains a safe, orderly, and respectful learning environment. It affirms the College’s commitment to fostering personal responsibility, self-discipline, and respect for others within a community grounded in the Catholic faith and moral tradition.
This Policy also establishes the College’s commitment to procedural fairness in the management of student behaviour. It ensures that students are treated with dignity and equity, that expectations are clearly communicated, and that decisions relating to student behaviour are made in a consistent, reasonable, and transparent manner.
This Policy further provides the framework for the fair investigation and resolution of student behaviour concerns, whether raised by complaint, staff observation, parent report, student report, or otherwise brought to the attention of the School. The College recognises that behaviour concerns may vary in seriousness, context, and impact, and that responses should be proportionate, educative, and directed towards the wellbeing of students and the safety and orderly operation of the School.
This Policy is developed in accordance with the requirements of the Education and Training Reform Regulations 2017 (Vic), including the minimum standards relating to student behaviour management.
Scope
This Policy applies to:
all students enrolled at Rosewood College
all staff responsible for the care, supervision, and management of students
all activities conducted under the authority of the College
This Policy applies to student behaviour in all contexts where a student is:
attending the College during normal school hours
participating in school activities, including excursions, camps, and co-curricular programs
representing the College in any capacity
travelling to or from the College where there is a connection to the school environment
engaging in online or digital environments where the behaviour has a direct impact on the safety, wellbeing, or reputation of students, staff, or the College
This Policy operates in conjunction with:
Student Behaviour Management Procedure
Suspension and Expulsion Procedure
Behaviour Incident Recording Procedure
Anti-Bullying and Harassment Policy
Anti-Bullying and Harassment Procedure
Uniform Policy and Uniform Guidelines
Enrolment Policy and Enrolment Agreement
Complaints and Grievances Policy
Policy
Behavioural Expectations and Formation
Rosewood College establishes clear expectations for student behaviour that promote a safe, orderly, and respectful learning environment.
Student behaviour is understood as an integral part of the formation of the whole person. The College seeks to support students in the development of virtues such as responsibility, respect, self-discipline, and consideration for others, consistent with its educational philosophy grounded in the Catholic faith and moral tradition.
Students are expected to:
act with respect towards all members of the school community
contribute positively to the learning environment
take responsibility for their actions and their impact on others
comply with College rules, policies, and reasonable directions from staff
Students are also expected to understand that their behaviour may have consequences for the safety, wellbeing, and learning of others, as well as for the reputation and orderly functioning of the school community.
Positive Behaviour and Preventative Approach
The College adopts a proactive and educative approach to behaviour management, with an emphasis on:
promoting positive behaviour
recognising and reinforcing appropriate conduct
supporting students to develop self-regulation and sound judgement
addressing behaviour concerns early and constructively
The College works in partnership with parents and guardians to support consistent expectations and the development of positive student behaviour.
Behaviour Management Principles
In responding to student behaviour concerns, the College:
treats all concerns seriously and appropriately, having regard to their nature, context, and impact
recognises that behaviour concerns may range from minor to very serious, and that responses should be proportionate to the circumstances
investigates and respond to concerns where appropriate, whether or not a formal complaint has been made
acts as promptly as reasonably practicable
applies the principles of procedural fairness
maintains confidentiality to the extent reasonably possible, having regard to the need to investigate and resolve the matter properly, protect safety and wellbeing, and comply with legal obligations
has regard to the age, maturity, individual circumstances, and wellbeing of the student
seeks, where appropriate, to combine disciplinary responses with educative, pastoral, and restorative measures
Prohibition of Corporal Punishment
Rosewood College does not permit or sanction corporal punishment of students in any circumstances.
Corporal punishment must not be administered by any staff member, volunteer, contractor, parent, guardian, or any other person for the purpose of enforcing discipline, or any other reason, at the College.
This prohibition applies to all behaviour management practices and operates in conjunction with this Policy, the Student Behaviour Management Procedure, and related student safety and wellbeing policies.
Fair and Consistent Management of Behaviour
Student behaviour is managed in a manner that is:
fair and proportionate
consistent across the College
responsive to the age, maturity, and individual circumstances of the student
directed towards the development and wellbeing of the student
mindful of the rights, safety, and wellbeing of other students, staff, and members of the school community
The College recognises that behaviour concerns may vary significantly in seriousness, context, frequency, and impact. Accordingly, the process followed and any response or consequence imposed may differ depending on the nature of the behaviour, the surrounding circumstances, any prior concerns, the needs of those affected, and the need to protect the safety, wellbeing, and orderly operation of the College.
The College may implement appropriate consequences where behaviour does not meet expectations. Such consequences are determined having regard to the nature, seriousness, and context of the behaviour, and may be accompanied by supportive or restorative measures where appropriate.
Procedural Fairness
Rosewood College is committed to the principles of procedural fairness in all matters relating to student behaviour.
This includes ensuring that:
students are aware of behavioural expectations and relevant policies
allegations of, or concerns about inappropriate behaviour are communicated clearly, where appropriate having regard to the age of the student and the circumstances of the matter
students are given a reasonable opportunity to respond to concerns raised
decisions are made by an appropriately authorised person
decisions are based on relevant information and made in a reasonable and transparent manner
significant behaviour matters are handled in a manner that is fair, timely, and proportionate
Procedural fairness applies to all behaviour management processes, including those that may result in significant disciplinary action.
Where a student is required to attend a formal meeting in relation to a significant behaviour concern or possible disciplinary action, the student may be accompanied by a parent, guardian, or other support person, subject to the College’s reasonable requirements for the proper conduct of the meeting. A support person is present to provide support and does not ordinarily act as an advocate unless the College permits otherwise.
Investigation and Response
Where concerns arise regarding student behaviour, the College may make such inquiries as it considers appropriate in the circumstances. This may include gathering relevant information, speaking with staff and students involved, obtaining written accounts, reviewing available records or other relevant material, and meeting with the student concerned.
The College may investigate and respond to alleged inappropriate behaviour whether the matter is raised by formal complaint, informal report, staff observation, or otherwise comes to the attention of the College.
The nature and extent of any investigation, and the process followed, depends on the seriousness and circumstances of the matter, including any issues of confidentiality, safety, wellbeing, and the number of students involved.
Where appropriate, the student is informed of the substance of the concern and given an opportunity to respond before a decision is made.
Nothing in this Policy prevents the College from taking immediate action where reasonably necessary to protect the safety, wellbeing, or orderly operation of the College pending further inquiry or determination.
Where alleged behaviour may involve unlawful conduct or present a serious risk to health, safety, or wellbeing, the College may refer the matter to external authorities or seek external advice, as appropriate.
Disciplinary Action
The College may take disciplinary action where a student’s behaviour does not meet expected standards.
Disciplinary action may include a range of responses appropriate to the circumstances, including, where necessary:
counselling, guidance, or restorative action
removal from class or temporary withdrawal from a particular setting or activity (e.g., lunchtime/after-school detention)
internal or external suspension
expulsion from the College
All disciplinary actions are undertaken in accordance with this Policy and the relevant procedures, including the Suspension and Expulsion Procedure.
Where appropriate, disciplinary responses may be accompanied by pastoral, wellbeing, behavioural support, or restorative measures aimed at assisting the student to reflect, repair harm, and re-engage positively with the life of the College.
The Principal may take immediate interim action, including removal from class, withdrawal from an activity, or suspension in accordance with the relevant procedure, where this is reasonably necessary to protect the safety, wellbeing, or orderly operation of the College pending further inquiry.
Roles and Responsibilities
The Principal is responsible for ensuring that student behaviour is managed in accordance with this Policy and that appropriate procedures are in place and implemented consistently.
The Principal, or an appropriately authorised delegate, is responsible for:
overseeing significant behaviour matters and disciplinary processes
ensuring that investigations and decisions are conducted fairly and in accordance with this Policy
determining appropriate responses in serious matters, including suspension or recommendation of expulsion where applicable under the relevant procedure
ensuring that proper records are maintained
Staff are responsible for:
promoting and modelling expected standards of behaviour
supporting students in meeting behavioural expectations
applying this Policy and associated procedures consistently and fairly
Staff are also responsible for:
responding to behaviour concerns in a timely, proportionate, and appropriate manner
reporting significant or repeated behaviour concerns, or behaviour that may give rise to serious disciplinary action, in accordance with College procedures
maintaining appropriate records in accordance with College procedures
Parent(s)/Guardian(s) are expected to:
support the College’s behavioural expectations
work in partnership with the College to address behaviour concerns
Parent(s)/Guardian(s) are also expected to participate, where appropriate, in meetings or processes relating to significant behaviour matters involving their child.
Students are responsible for:
meeting the behavioural expectations of the College
responding positively to guidance and direction from staff
Students are also responsible for participating honestly and respectfully in behaviour management processes.
Relationship to Other Policies and Procedures
This Policy is supported by, and should be read in conjunction with, the College’s behaviour management procedures and related policies, including those addressing:
behaviour management processes
suspension and expulsion
bullying and harassment
student safety and wellbeing
These documents provide the operational detail for the implementation of this Policy.
Implementation
The Principal is responsible for the implementation of this Policy and for ensuring that student behaviour is managed in a manner consistent with the College’s educational philosophy, this Policy, and applicable regulatory requirements.
The Principal ensures that:
appropriate procedures are established and maintained to support the implementation of this Policy, including:
Student Behaviour Management Procedure
Suspension and Expulsion Procedure
Behaviour Incident Recording Procedure
expectations of student behaviour are clearly communicated to students, staff, and parent(s)/guardian(s)
staff are supported and trained to apply behaviour management practices consistently and in accordance with this Policy
systems are in place for the recording, monitoring, and review of student behaviour, including behavioural incidents, investigations, supports implemented, suspensions, and expulsions
behaviour management practices are regularly monitored to ensure consistency, fairness, and alignment with the College’s values
Staff are responsible for:
implementing this Policy and associated procedures in their day-to-day interactions with students
modelling appropriate behaviour and reinforcing College expectations
responding to behaviour concerns in a timely, consistent, and proportionate manner
maintaining appropriate records in accordance with College procedures
Staff must also treat behaviour matters confidentially, except to the extent disclosure is necessary to investigate and resolve the matter properly, support student wellbeing, or meet legal obligations.
The College maintains appropriate records of student behaviour incidents, investigations, meetings, supports implemented, disciplinary decisions, and outcomes as evidence of the consistent application of this Policy and to support ongoing monitoring and review. Where relevant, records are retained on the student’s file in accordance with College procedures and applicable privacy obligations.
The Governing Authority provides oversight of the College’s compliance with the minimum standards for school registration, including the effective implementation of this Policy.
Communication to the School Community
The College communicates student behaviour management expectations, policies, and procedures to the school community through appropriate channels, which may include:
enrolment materials, including the Enrolment Agreement
the Parent Handbook
student orientation and ongoing student reminders
staff induction, staff meetings, and professional learning
direct communication with parent(s)/guardian(s) where behaviour concerns arise
publication or access through the College’s approved document management or communication systems
The Principal is responsible for ensuring that student behaviour management policies and procedures are accessible to staff, students, and parent(s)/guardian(s), and that key expectations are communicated in a clear and age-appropriate manner.
Review
This Policy will be reviewed at least every two years, or earlier if required due to:
changes to legislation or regulatory requirements, including the Education and Training Reform Regulations 2017 (Vic)
changes to College operations or behaviour management practices
identified issues arising from the implementation or monitoring of this Policy
direction from the Governing Authority
The Principal is responsible for initiating the review of this Policy.
The Governing Authority is responsible for the approval of any amendments.

Student Code of Conduct Policy

## Suspension and Expulsion Procedure

Exported on 30 Jun 2026
Purpose
The purpose of this Procedure is to define how Rosewood College manages serious breaches of student behaviour that may result in suspension or expulsion, in accordance with the Student Behaviour Management Policy.
This Procedure establishes a clear, fair, and consistent process for:
considering and applying suspension or expulsion
ensuring that decisions are made in a manner that is reasonable, proportionate, and evidence-based
upholding the principles of procedural fairness in all disciplinary decisions
This Procedure supports the College’s commitment to maintaining a safe and orderly learning environment while recognising the dignity of each student and the importance of just and transparent decision-making.
Scope
This Procedure applies to:
all students enrolled at Rosewood College
the Principal and any delegated staff responsible for decisions relating to suspension or expulsion
staff involved in the management, investigation, and documentation of serious behaviour incidents
This Procedure applies in circumstances where a student’s behaviour:
constitutes a serious breach of the College’s behavioural expectations
poses a risk to the safety or wellbeing of students, staff, or others
involves repeated or persistent non-compliance with College expectations
may warrant disciplinary action beyond routine behaviour management responses
This Procedure applies to behaviour occurring:
at the College
during activities conducted under the authority of the College, including excursions, camps, and co-curricular programs
when a student is representing the College
in online or digital environments where the behaviour has a direct impact on the school community
This Procedure operates in conjunction with:
Student Behaviour Management Policy
Student Behaviour Management Procedure
Behaviour Incident Recording Procedure
Enrolment Policy and Enrolment Agreement
This Procedure is to be read alongside the College’s obligations relating to procedural fairness and student wellbeing.
Procedure
Identification and Initial Response
Where a serious behaviour incident occurs, or where a pattern of behaviour gives rise to concern, the matter is escalated to the Principal or delegated staff member.
An initial assessment is undertaken to:
establish the nature and seriousness of the behaviour
identify any immediate risks to the safety or wellbeing of students, staff, or others
determine whether immediate action is required, including temporary removal from class or the school environment
Where necessary to ensure safety or to support a fair process, a student may be temporarily removed from normal activities while the matter is considered.
Consideration of Disciplinary Action
Where suspension or expulsion is being considered, the College:
identify the relevant behaviour, rules, or expectations alleged to have been breached
gather and consider relevant information and evidence
assess the seriousness and context of the behaviour
consider the student’s individual circumstances, including age, maturity, and any relevant background factors
The College determines whether suspension or expulsion is an appropriate and proportionate response in the circumstances.
Procedural Fairness
Before a decision is made to suspend or expel a student, the College ensures that procedural fairness is afforded.
This includes:
informing the student and parent(s)/guardian(s) of the concerns and the allegations being considered
providing sufficient detail to enable a meaningful response
providing the student and parent(s)/guardian(s) with an opportunity to respond, either verbally or in writing
ensuring that decisions are made by an impartial and appropriately authorised person
considering all relevant information before making a final decision
Where expulsion is being considered, the College provides an opportunity for a meeting with the student and parent(s)/guardian(s), and may allow a support person to be present.
Decision-Making
Following consideration of all relevant information, the Principal (or delegated authority) determines the appropriate outcome.
In making a decision, the College has regard to:
the safety and wellbeing of students, staff, and the school community
the seriousness of the behaviour
any previous behaviour of the student
the response of the student, including any acknowledgement or remorse
the student’s prospects for improvement and continued participation in the College
The decision is documented and communicated to the student and parent(s)/guardian(s).
Outcomes
Outcomes may include:
no further disciplinary action, with or without additional support measures
implementation of alternative behaviour management strategies
suspension for a specified period
expulsion from the College
Where a suspension is imposed, the College determines:
the duration of the suspension
whether the suspension is internal or external
any conditions associated with the suspension
Expulsion is considered a serious and final measure and is only applied where it is determined to be appropriate in the circumstances.
Communication of Decision
The College communicates decisions relating to suspension or expulsion:
verbally where appropriate
in writing to parent(s)/guardian(s), outlining:
the decision
the reasons for the decision
the duration where relevant
any conditions or expectations arising from the decision
any re-entry requirements
The College maintains records of all decisions and communications in accordance with the Behaviour Incident Recording Procedure.
Re-Entry Following Suspension
Where a student returns to the College following a suspension, the College may require a re-entry process.
This may include:
a meeting with the student and parent(s)/guardian(s)
clarification of expectations for behaviour
agreement on any support or conditions for return
The purpose of the re-entry process is to support the student’s successful return to the College and to promote ongoing positive behaviour.
Records and Registers
All suspensions and expulsions are recorded by the College in accordance with the Suspension and Expulsion Register Procedure.
Records relating to suspension or expulsion decisions include, where applicable:
details of the incident and decision
evidence considered
communications with the student and parent(s)/guardian(s)
outcomes and any conditions imposed
re-entry arrangements, where applicable
The Suspension and Expulsion Register is maintained in accordance with regulatory requirements and the College’s record management obligations.
Implementation
Responsibility for Implementation
The Principal is responsible for the implementation of this Procedure and for ensuring that all decisions relating to suspension and expulsion are made in accordance with this Procedure, the Student Behaviour Management Policy, and applicable regulatory requirements.
The Principal may delegate aspects of the implementation of this Procedure to appropriately authorised staff, while retaining overall responsibility for decision-making and compliance.
Staff Responsibilities
Staff are responsible for:
identifying and reporting serious behaviour concerns in a timely manner
supporting the investigation and documentation of incidents
implementing interim measures as directed to ensure safety and support procedural fairness
participating in meetings and processes associated with behaviour management where required
Staff must ensure that all actions taken are consistent with this Procedure and that appropriate records are maintained.
Documentation and Record Management
The College maintains appropriate documentation in relation to all matters involving suspension and expulsion.
This includes:
records of incidents and investigations
records of communication with students and parent(s)/guardian(s)
documentation of decisions and outcomes
records of re-entry processes where applicable
Records are maintained in accordance with the Behaviour Incident Recording Procedure and relevant College record management requirements.
Monitoring and Compliance
The Principal is responsible for monitoring the application of this Procedure to ensure:
decisions are made consistently and in accordance with procedural fairness
disciplinary actions are appropriate and proportionate
regulatory requirements are met
The Governing Authority oversees the College’s compliance with the minimum standards for school registration, including the effective implementation of this Procedure.
Review
This Procedure will be reviewed at least every two years, or earlier if required due to:
changes to legislation or regulatory requirements, including the Education and Training Reform Regulations 2017 (Vic)
changes to College operations or behaviour management practices
identified issues arising from the implementation of this Procedure
direction from the Principal or Governing Authority
The Principal is responsible for initiating and overseeing the review of this Procedure.

## Complaints and Grievances Policy

Exported on 30 Jun 2026
Purpose
The Complaints and Grievances Policy establishes Rosewood College’s commitment to receiving, managing and resolving complaints and grievances in a fair, respectful, timely and child-safe manner.
This policy supports the school’s duty of care, child safety obligations, parent and guardian engagement, student wellbeing, staff accountability and continuous improvement.
The policy also supports a child-safe culture by ensuring students and families can raise concerns, including child safety concerns, in ways that are accessible, culturally safe, taken seriously and responded to promptly.
Rosewood College recognises that complaints and grievances can identify risks, misunderstandings, unmet needs, procedural concerns or opportunities to improve College operations.
This policy reflects Rosewood College’s identity as an independent school grounded in the Catholic faith and moral tradition, recognising the dignity of each person and the responsibility to act with justice, charity, honesty and care.
Scope
This policy applies to:
the Governing Authority
the Principal
all staff
students
parents and guardians
volunteers
contractors
external providers
visitors
other members of the school community, where relevant
This policy applies to complaints and grievances relating to Rosewood College, including concerns about:
student care, safety or welfare
child safety
student learning or participation
staff conduct
student behaviour
bullying, harassment or discrimination
first aid, medical support or student wellbeing
supervision
excursions and offsite activities
external providers
privacy or records handling
communication with the school
College operations, procedures or decisions
conduct of volunteers, contractors, external providers or visitors connected with school activities
This policy does not replace mandatory reporting, reportable conduct, child safety, emergency, privacy, employment, disciplinary or legal obligations. Where another procedure applies, that procedure must be followed in addition to this policy.
Complaints involving child safety must be managed as child safety matters first. They may also be managed as complaints under this policy, but complaint resolution must not delay immediate protective action, mandatory reporting, reportable conduct notification, police contact or other required escalation.
Legal and Regulatory Context
This policy supports Rosewood College’s compliance with applicable Victorian school registration, duty of care, child safety, privacy, anti-discrimination and governance obligations. It must be read together with the College’s Child Safety Policy, Child Safety Code of Conduct Policy, Mandatory Reporting Policy, Reportable Conduct Scheme Procedure, Privacy Policy and Records Management Policy. Where a complaint raises a child safety, mandatory reporting, reportable conduct, emergency, employment, privacy or legal issue, the relevant specific procedure must be followed.
Policy
Complaint Pathways and Contact Points
Complaints and grievances may be raised verbally or in writing. Students may raise a concern with the Principal, a teacher, a staff member they trust, a parent or guardian who then contacts the College, or another authorised person identified by the College.
Parents and guardians may raise concerns with the relevant teacher, the Principal or the College office, depending on the nature and seriousness of the concern.
Serious complaints, child safety concerns, reportable conduct concerns, safety risks and urgent wellbeing matters must be escalated immediately to the Principal or other authorised person.
Complaints about the Principal must be referred to the Chairman of the Governing Authority or another person authorised by the Governing Authority. Complaints about the Chairman of the Governing Authority must be referred to another authorised member of the Governing Authority or handled in accordance with the Governance Charter.
Commitment to Fair and Safe Complaint Handling
Rosewood College is committed to managing complaints and grievances in a way that is:
respectful
accessible
child-focused
timely
procedurally fair
confidential where appropriate
responsive to safety and wellbeing risks
consistent with privacy and records obligations
directed towards resolution, accountability and improvement
free of charge for complainants
Complaints and grievances must be taken seriously and must not be dismissed because they are informal, verbal, raised by a student, raised by a parent or guardian, or expressed as concern rather than a formal complaint.
Definition of Complaint
A complaint is an expression of dissatisfaction about Rosewood College, a school decision, action, omission, service, process, staff member, student, volunteer, contractor, external provider or other person connected with the school, where a response or resolution is expected.
A complaint may be made verbally or in writing.
A complaint may be made formally or informally.
Definition of Grievance
A grievance is a complaint or concern where the person raising the matter believes they have been personally affected by a decision, action, omission, conduct, process or unresolved concern.
A grievance may involve student welfare, family concerns, staff interaction, school decision-making, procedural fairness, communication, safety, privacy or another matter affecting a person’s relationship with the school.
Complaints from Students
Rosewood College supports students to raise concerns and complaints in ways that are suitable to their age, maturity, communication needs and circumstances. Students may raise concerns directly or through a trusted adult without fear of disadvantage. Support is provided where required to ensure students can communicate concerns effectively, including consideration of communication needs or reasonable adjustments.
Students may raise concerns with:
the Principal
a teacher
a staff member they trust
a parent or guardian who then contacts the school
another authorised person identified by the school
A student who raises a complaint, or who is involved in a complaint, will continue to participate in learning and school activities unless a temporary change is necessary for safety, wellbeing, supervision, legal or child safety reasons.
Staff must respond to student complaints and concerns respectfully and must consider whether the matter involves safety, wellbeing, child safety, bullying, harassment, behaviour, staff conduct or another risk requiring immediate action.
Complaints from Parents, Guardians and Community Members
Parents, guardians and other members of the school community may raise complaints or grievances with Rosewood College.
The school encourages concerns to be raised early where this may assist resolution.
Parents and guardians must communicate respectfully and constructively with staff, and must not take action that compromises student safety, privacy, procedural fairness or the wellbeing of others.
Complaints Involving Child Safety
Complaints or concerns involving child safety must be prioritised and escalated immediately to the Principal or Governing Authority.
This includes complaints or concerns involving:
child abuse or suspected child abuse
grooming
sexualised behaviour or sexual harassment
serious peer-to-peer harm
adult conduct towards a student
family violence concern
serious neglect
failure to protect a student from serious risk
inappropriate staff, volunteer, contractor, visitor or external provider conduct
reportable conduct concern
online child safety concern
any matter suggesting that a student may be at risk of significant harm
Child safety reporting obligations are not displaced by this policy.
Staff who receive or become aware of a child safety concern must report it immediately through the College’s child safety reporting pathway and must not wait for a written complaint. The immediate safety of the student must be assessed and protective action taken where required.
Procedural Fairness
Rosewood College will apply procedural fairness when managing complaints and grievances.
Procedural fairness requires that, where appropriate and subject to safety, child safety, legal and privacy considerations:
the person raising the complaint is heard respectfully
the person who is the subject of the complaint is informed of relevant concerns at an appropriate level of detail
relevant information is considered before decisions are made
decisions are made without bias
conflicts of interest are identified and managed
outcomes are communicated in a fair and appropriate way
Procedural fairness does not prevent the school from taking immediate protective action where required for student safety, child safety or wellbeing.
Confidentiality and Privacy
Complaints and grievances must be handled confidentially and in accordance with the Privacy Policy and Records Management Policy.
Information must be shared only with persons who need it for complaint handling, student safety, child safety, legal, governance, operational or wellbeing reasons.
The College will not disclose personal information about students, families, staff or other persons unless authorised or required.
Where a complaint involves another student, parents and guardians must not expect access to private information about that student, including disciplinary action or personal circumstances.
The College takes reasonable steps to ensure that a student, parent, guardian, staff member or other person is not disadvantaged for raising a genuine concern or participating in complaint handling.
No Victimisation or Retaliation
Rosewood College does not tolerate victimisation or retaliation against a person who raises a complaint, supports another person to raise a complaint, provides information, or participates in a complaint handling process.
Any allegation of retaliation must be taken seriously, recorded and assessed for student safety, child safety, staff conduct, behaviour management or complaint escalation.
Accessible Complaint Handling
Rosewood College takes reasonable steps to make complaint handling accessible to students, parents, guardians and members of the school community.
This may include:
providing child-friendly explanations of complaint pathways
ensuring complaint handling is culturally safe for Aboriginal students and families and respectful of diverse cultural and family contexts
helping students understand how to raise concerns
receiving complaints verbally or in writing
providing support to students who need assistance to raise a concern
offering reasonable assistance where language, literacy, disability or age affects a person’s ability to raise a complaint
considering communication needs
allowing a support person where appropriate
providing information in a way that is reasonably understandable
supporting Aboriginal students and families to raise concerns safely and respectfully
supporting students with disability or additional needs to raise concerns
Early Resolution
Where appropriate and safe, Rosewood College seeks to resolve complaints at the earliest suitable level.
Early resolution may involve:
clarifying the concern
providing information
correcting a misunderstanding
apologising where appropriate
taking immediate practical action
adjusting communication
agreeing on next steps
referring the matter to the appropriate staff member or procedure
Early resolution must not be used to minimise, avoid or delay response to serious complaints, child safety concerns, reportable conduct concerns, safety risks, privacy breaches, repeated issues or matters requiring formal review.
Where appropriate, the outcome communication must identify the issue considered, the process followed, the outcome or action to be taken, any limits on what can be disclosed, and any available internal review or escalation pathway.
Withdrawal of Complaints
A complainant may withdraw a complaint at any time. The College may still need to continue considering or acting on the matter where it raises student safety, child safety, legal, governance, staff conduct, repeated pattern or operational risk.
Joint or Repeated Complaints
Where multiple people raise substantially the same issue, the College may manage the concerns together where this is fair, efficient and does not compromise confidentiality, student safety or procedural fairness.
Formal Complaint Handling
Formal complaint handling is required where a complaint is serious, unresolved, repeated, complex, involves safety or child safety, involves staff conduct, requires investigation, requires procedural fairness, or cannot be resolved informally.
Formal complaint handling must be documented and must include:
receipt of the complaint
assessment of the concern
allocation of responsibility
consideration of immediate safety or wellbeing needs
consideration of child safety and reporting obligations
communication with relevant parties
information gathering where required
decision or outcome
corrective action where required
review or escalation options where appropriate
records retained in approved systems
Internal Review and Escalation
A complainant may request internal review where they believe the complaint process was not followed, relevant information was not considered, the outcome was not reasonably open on the information available, or a conflict of interest affected the process. In response, the Principal, or another authorised person where the Principal has a conflict, determines the appropriate review pathway. Internal review does not prevent the College from taking immediate protective, child safety, legal, employment or operational action where required.
External Agencies and Referral
Where appropriate, complainants may be directed to relevant external agencies. This may include Victoria Police in an emergency or where a crime may have occurred, Child Protection for mandatory reporting concerns, the Social Services Regulator/Commission for Children and Young People for child safety or reportable conduct matters, the VRQA for school registration complaints, or other bodies relevant to the issue. The College may also be required to report matters externally. External referral or reporting does not prevent the College from taking immediate steps to protect students and manage risk.
Complaints About the Principal
A complaint about the Principal must be referred to the Chairman of the Governing Authority or another person authorised by the Governing Authority.
The Principal must not manage a complaint where they are the subject of the complaint or where there is an actual or perceived conflict of interest that cannot be managed.
Complaints About the Governing Authority
A complaint about a member of the Governing Authority must be referred to the Chairman of the Governing Authority, unless the complaint concerns theChairman.
A complaint about the Chairman of the Governing Authority must be referred to another authorised member of the Governing Authority or handled in accordance with the Governance Charter.
Anonymous Complaints
Rosewood College may consider anonymous complaints where sufficient information is provided to enable assessment or action.
The College may be limited in its ability to investigate or respond to an anonymous complaint, but must still consider whether the complaint raises a student safety, child safety, legal, operational or governance risk.
A person may request that their identity be treated confidentially. The College considers such requests, however confidentiality may be limited where information must be shared for safety, child safety, legal, procedural fairness, reporting or investigation reasons
Unreasonable Complainant Conduct
Rosewood College treats complainants respectfully, but may manage unreasonable conduct to protect students, staff and College operations.
Unreasonable conduct may include:
abusive, threatening or aggressive communication
repeated contact that is disproportionate to the issue
refusal to engage with reasonable process
repeated re-raising of matters already addressed without new information
conduct that breaches privacy or procedural fairness
direct contact with other students, parents or staff in a way that compromises safety or fairness
Any restriction on communication must be reasonable, proportionate and approved by the Principal or Governing Authority where appropriate. Any decision to limit communication should be reviewed periodically and should not prevent a person from raising new, serious or child safety concerns.
Records and Continuous Improvement
Rosewood College maintains records of complaints and grievances. Records may include the complaint received, date, parties involved, risk assessment, child safety or external reporting considerations, actions taken, communications, outcome, reasons where appropriate, corrective actions, review requests and closure date.
Complaint records must support:
fair handling
accountability
student safety and wellbeing
child safety reporting
procedural fairness
privacy and confidentiality
communication with parties
corrective action
pattern review
governance oversight
evidence readiness
The College reviews complaint information to identify recurring concerns, systemic issues, unresolved risks and opportunities for improvement.
Implementation
The Governing Authority is responsible for approving this policy and maintaining oversight of complaint handling as part of the College’s governance, child safety and duty of care arrangements.
The Principal is responsible for implementing this policy and ensuring that Rosewood College has practical arrangements for receiving, assessing, managing, recording, escalating and reviewing complaints and grievances.
The Principal must ensure that:
this policy is communicated to staff
complaint pathways are communicated to students, parents and guardians
complaints and grievances are taken seriously
child safety complaints are escalated through required pathways
complaint records are maintained in approved systems
privacy and confidentiality are managed
conflicts of interest are identified and managed
serious or systemic complaints are escalated to the Governing Authority where required
complaints are reviewed to identify risk, corrective action and improvement opportunities
The Principal provides the Governing Authority with periodic or annual de-identified reporting on complaints trends, serious complaints, systemic issues and improvement actions, while maintaining privacy and confidentiality
Staff are responsible for:
listening respectfully to concerns
responding promptly where a matter is within their role
escalating serious, unresolved or sensitive matters
reporting child safety concerns immediately
maintaining confidentiality
creating records where required
following the Complaints and Grievances Procedure
Students, parents, guardians and members of the school community are encouraged to raise concerns promptly and communicate respectfully during complaint handling.
Review
This policy must be reviewed at least every two years, or earlier if required.
This policy must also be reviewed when there is:
a serious complaint or grievance indicating that complaint handling arrangements may be ineffective
a child safety complaint or reportable conduct concern
a pattern of repeated complaints
a complaint involving procedural fairness, privacy, student safety or governance risk
a change to the Complaints and Grievances Procedure
a material change to child safety, duty of care, privacy, records management, behaviour management, staff conduct or governance requirements
a change to legislation, Ministerial Orders, VRQA guidance or registration expectations
a VRQA review, audit or registration process identifying a relevant issue
a governance review indicating that this policy is unclear, incomplete or ineffective
The Principal is responsible for coordinating review of this policy.
Material amendments must be approved by the Governing Authority.
